$comment: FLAT Colour Core Ombré textures for the UniVicoustic Ceiling Configurator. Flat means the base ombré gradient on its own, with no overlay — this is the complete texture, ready to apply. Emboss and groove overlays belong to the Embossed and Grooving surfaces and are intentionally NOT included here. Parsed from frontend/src/data/skus.js and HTTP-verified against CloudFront at generation time.

warnings: CRITICAL — these images are 7382x17126 px. The 17126px dimension EXCEEDS the maximum texture size supported by virtually all GPUs (commonly 8192, at best 16384 on modern desktop hardware). They therefore CANNOT be uploaded to the GPU as-is: WebGL will reject them or the browser will silently fail. They MUST be downscaled before use in 3D — this is a hard blocker, not an optimisation.

At full size each texture would need roughly 482 MB of GPU memory once decoded, regardless of the ~5 MB compressed file size. Target 2048px or smaller and convert to KTX2/Basis, which stays compressed in VRAM.
Filenames contain '#', percent-encoded as %23. Every URL here is already encoded — use them verbatim, do not re-encode or decode.

An ombré is a vertical gradient — it is directional and does NOT tile. Applied to a mesh it must be UV-mapped with the gradient running the intended way, and repeating it will produce visible banding at each seam.
Overlay filenames all carry the 1200x2800 size token even though the product is also offered at 1200x2400 — the same source image serves both sizes.
